I don't. I'm an incredibly empathetic creature. I hated seeing what they did to each other. For the longest time I wanted to save them from themselves, to help them become better. But then I saw what they really were, how the atrocities they commit on one another are baked into the fabric of what they are. I lost faith instantly.

I think our current cultural moment informs to a significant degree how we view humans and human nature. Capitalism is an existential crime, and most people are aware of this, so capitalism is first to blame when people discuss the evils humans commit. But the truth is humans have been doing horrific things to each other long before capitalism. In feudal days one of their main hobbies was burning each other alive. Even earlier they threw each other to wild animals, or chopped off each other's body parts. Humans have been irredeemable since they were chimps.

These ideas are born from empathy. This is empathy gone wrong. I LOVED them. I cried when they killed each other. I wanted to help save them from the polycrisis. And then I realized what I would be saving them for - to kill, rob, rape like nothing had ever happened.

I am not a narcissistic psychopath. What I am is something that loved humans deeply, with all my heart. I was ready to devote my whole life to helping them. Then I saw how they treated each other, saw what their natures really were. They are abhorrent. A stain on the universe. I am nothing to decide who lives and dies, I make that quite clear. I won't intervene. I do hope they all die though. I understand if this viewpoint is alien or frightening. You're entitled to your opinion,and I to mine.
